page: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is an Env6 family network-optimized server instance. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32ns_v6 demonstrates strong performance in memory bandwidth for large block read-only operations, reaching 192.86 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU physics tests also rank in the top 25% tier. For language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M models at 381.68 tokens/sec, and strong performance in prompt processing for medium 7B models. However, text generation for large 70B models is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25% at 2.56 tokens/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU and network-optimized design, the E32ns_v6 offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of local storage. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) enhances its efficiency for vector and matrix mathematics, making it a viable option for memory-heavy enterprise applications and data processing pipelines.
